config.providers.description: Configured model provider list (API keys excluded; keys are kept in secure storage)
config.activeProvider.description: Alias of the currently active model provider
config.backgroundProvider.description: Provider alias used for background tasks (turn summaries / session archiving / polishing / deduplication). Empty = same as live chat. User-level preference: follows the user, not the project. Requires a window reload to take effect
config.showMetrics.description: Show activity metrics (LLM call count / tool failures and truncations / tokens / security audit / fingerprint hashes and other diagnostic info). Hidden by default because it is noise for regular users; enable it when you need debugging observability
config.attentionSound.description: Interaction alert sound: when the chat panel is not in the foreground, a system sound plays for approval cards, pending AI questions, and turn completion. Disabled = fully muted (in-panel badges and unread state still work). Takes effect immediately.
config.allowedPaths.description: Extra directories allowed by the whitelist (trusted directories outside the project root that the agent may read and write). The project root is always allowed and needs no entry. User-level: machine-wide directory trust, so personal absolute paths never enter project settings. Takes effect immediately and survives restarts.
config.searchEngine.description: Backend used by the internal web_search tool. Values: auto (default Bing→DuckDuckGo chain), bing, duckduckgo, baidu, sogou, or a custom search engine name (defined in the settings panel under "Custom search engines"). User-level preference: follows the user, not the project. Requires a window reload to take effect.
config.archiveMode.description: Session archive mode. full = automatic: generate a session summary and topics when switching or forking away from a session (used by history search); manual = only on explicit user action. Turn summaries are unaffected by this setting (always generated). User-level preference: follows the user, not the project. The settings panel applies changes immediately (the kernel refuses to switch mid-conversation; the preference is saved and applied once the conversation ends).
config.customSearchEngines.description: User-defined web search engines (backend of the web_search tool). Each entry = name + URL template (?q={query}) + a host-preset parse strategy. Only structured result sources are supported; custom HTML parsing is not available (security red line). Requires a window reload to take effect.
config.customSearchEngines.name.descript: Engine display name (unique; used as the selector value)
config.customSearchEngines.urlTemplate.d: Search URL template; use {query} as the query placeholder (e.g. https://example.com/search?q={query})
config.customSearchEngines.parseStrategy: Result parse strategy (host-preset; custom parsing logic is not allowed). openSearchRss = OpenSearch RSS/Atom; jsonApi = JSON search API (expects {results:[{title,url,snippet}]} or {items:[...]})
config.scriptNodePath.description: Absolute path to the node executable used for script execution (optional). Used by node scripts of run_skill_script / run_project_script; when empty, node is looked up on the system PATH. Set this when the host machine has no standalone node (skill scripts fail with ENOENT), for example the node path of a bundled runtime. Requires a window reload to take effect.
config.disabledSkills.description: List of disabled skill names (configuration-style enable/disable). Scope = the global skill pool (built-in + user skills); skills embedded in an active role pack follow a separate "activated with the role" semantic and are unaffected. A matched skill does not exist from the model's point of view: it is excluded from the skill list, read_skill cannot read it, and L3 resources and scripts are unreachable. The Skills page still lists the entry with a "Disabled" badge (so you can confirm the setting took effect; it never silently disappears). Skill name = the name shown in the skill list (Agent Skills spec: kebab-case, e.g. code-review). User-level preference: follows the user, not the project. Takes effect immediately — synced to the kernel, with the Skills page and the chat skill dropdown refreshed automatically, no window reload or manual reload needed.
config.mcpServers.description: MCP server list (Model Context Protocol: connect external tool servers). User-level setting: follows the user, not the project — a workspace-level config could be committed by someone else and auto-launch arbitrary commands, so it is not offered. The stdio transport launches a local subprocess: only add servers you trust. The http transport sends tool arguments and results to the configured domain (data egress): again, only add services you trust. Once connected, its tools appear in the tool list as mcp__<server>__<tool> and require user confirmation on every call by default (exempt individual tools or a whole server in memora.mcpToolAllowlist; an audit record is still written). Read-only hints declared by the server itself are not treated as trusted. Takes effect immediately — servers are started and stopped incrementally by name (add / disable / change args / clear all need no window reload); see docs/mcp-setup.md. Scope machine: user settings only, not synced by VS Code Settings Sync (configure once per machine).
config.mcpServers.name.description: Server name (unique). Used as the tool name prefix mcp__<name>__<tool> and as the addressing key for disabling and logs
config.mcpServers.transport.description: Transport type (defaults to stdio). stdio = launch a local subprocess (command required); http = connect to a remote Streamable HTTP server (url required, headers optional). The two transports have mutually exclusive fields; mixing them reports an incomplete configuration. SSE is decided against
config.mcpServers.command.description: Executable command that launches the MCP server (e.g. node, npx, python). Required when transport is absent or stdio
config.mcpServers.url.description: Remote server address (required when transport: http). Only http/https is supported; non-local addresses must use https (http is allowed for loopback)
config.mcpServers.headers.description: Remote request headers (optional when transport: http). User-supplied and stored in plaintext with your settings: the machine scope only means it is not synced by VS Code Settings Sync — it is not encrypted storage, so any program that can read settings.json on this machine can see the values. This version has no SecretStorage-backed entry point, so do not put long-lived high-privilege tokens here; for servers that need OAuth or short-lived tokens, use your own proxy or skip them for now
config.mcpServers.env.description: Extra environment variables (optional). Merged over the default safe environment; on key conflicts the values here win
config.mcpServers.cwd.description: Working directory for the subprocess (optional; defaults to the extension host's)
config.mcpServers.enabled.description: Whether the server is enabled (defaults to enabled). Off = not launched and its tools do not exist for the model
config.mcpToolAllowlist.description: MCP tool confirmation allowlist (no prompt ≠ no audit: matches are still written to the audit log). Two key levels: per-tool mcp__<server>__<tool> (exempts that one tool) and per-server mcp__<server>__* (exempts every tool of that server). Note that the per-server level is a server-level authorization, not a snapshot of tool names: tools added to that server later fall inside the exemption automatically (a server upgrade that adds tools, or a different server reusing the same name), without asking you again. Tool names cannot be known in advance, so if you want new tools to still require confirmation you must exempt them one by one with per-tool keys. Both key levels address the server and the tool by their original names — if an original name contains `-`, `.` and the like, the sanitized display name (the one in the model's tool list) differs from the key, and writing the display name silently fails and falls back to confirming every call. There is no "exempt all servers at once" form: the server segment supports no wildcard, so exempting N servers takes N explicit keys. Match = that tool is called without a prompt but still audited; no match = every call asks. Takes effect immediately (tiers are recomputed; servers are not reconnected); see docs/mcp-setup.md. Scope machine (not synced by VS Code Settings Sync; configure once per machine).
